why.B1.1: Hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis are characteristic findings in primary aldosteronism, which is strongly supported by the low serum potassium level and elevated bicarbonate level.

fact_rationales.F13: Hypokalemia (low potassium) is a hallmark of primary aldosteronism, making this finding strongly supportive of this diagnosis.
fact_rationales.F14: Metabolic alkalosis, as suggested by elevated bicarbonate levels, can be seen in primary aldosteronism due to the effects of aldosterone on renal electrolyte handling.
fact_rationales.F3: Fatigue and muscle cramps can be seen in various conditions, but are more typical of primary aldosteronism and chronic kidney disease due to electrolyte imbalances and hypertension.
